scope: All 127 original headings reviewed; additional walkthroughs and planning references added.
method: Mechanics are paraphrased from linked sources. Editorial tips are recommendations and calculations, not developer promises or guaranteed outcomes. Wiki pages may be incomplete; named faction availability is not verified by a generic mechanics source.

sections.title: Welcome
facts: Torn permits one account per person; ownership and account-sharing restrictions matter from the start.
tips: Build a repeatable login routine: bars, education, job, cash and upcoming commitments.
Choose one short-term goal before spending; level 15, training and liquidity need different budgets.

sections.title: Donator Status
facts: Using a Donator Pack grants 31 donator days and 60 points; subscriptions are a different product.
tips: Compare the current pack price against the value of the benefits you will actually use.
Buy a pack with in-game cash if affordable; do not rely on old market-price quotes.

sections.title: Need Help? stuck somewhere?
facts: Official rules and help channels take precedence over player-written shortcuts.
tips: When asking for help, include your goal, level, the exact message and what you already tried.
Crop API keys, passwords, email addresses and session tokens out of screenshots.

sections.title: Go further
facts: Education unlocks lasting perks; gym progression rewards consistent training.
tips: Keep a small notebook of mistakes and one next action for each guide you finish.
Review your plan weekly instead of chasing every profitable-looking idea simultaneously.

introduction.summary: A practical start: protect your account, plan your resources and build a routine.
corrections: Do not confuse subscription rewards with using a tradable Donator Pack.
checklist: Read the game rules and secure your account.
Choose a goal and set a budget that leaves an emergency reserve.
Review bars, education and cash exposure at each normal login.

extras.title: Account and API-key hygiene
facts: Torn restricts software to authorised API data or the page a player manually loaded and is actively viewing.
tips: Use a dedicated, least-privilege key per trusted tool so one revocation does not disable every service.
Never copy a Torn password, browser cookie or another player's credentials into a helper.

sections.title: Sidebar Top
facts: The sidebar groups account actions, game areas and player lists.
tips: Read status tooltips before buying a cure or assuming a feature is broken.
Put frequently used pages in your own routine rather than opening every menu on each login.

sections.title: Icons
facts: Status icons distinguish ongoing effects and cooldowns.
tips: Check the relevant timer, not only the icon colour, before scheduling another action.
If an icon seems unfamiliar, inspect it in Torn before acting on a screenshot or cached observation.

sections.title: Money
facts: Cash on hand is the exposure relevant to mugging; total net worth is a different measure.
tips: Decide where proceeds will go before accepting a sale or withdrawing a balance.
Keep only your working float available and compare storage access times before committing funds.

sections.title: Level
facts: Experience is hidden; winning and leaving a higher-level opponent is a documented levelling route.
tips: A target's visible level does not prove it is weak; check your own attack results.
Accept an available upgrade when pursuing travel access rather than accidentally level-holding.

sections.title: Points
facts: Points buy unlocks and refills; they cannot be placed in an ordinary direct trade.
tips: List permanent unlocks and recurring refills separately in your budget.
Compare a refill's usable gain with its current point cost; avoid refilling an already-full bar.

sections.title: Merits
facts: Upgrade tiers become more expensive: a ten-tier merit line costs 55 merits in total.
tips: Choose upgrades that serve your current goal; early education reductions are a planning choice, not a universal rule.
Read reset costs and available free resets before experimenting with an expensive allocation.

sections.title: Energy
facts: Normal regeneration is 5 energy per 15 minutes to 100; donator regeneration is 5 per 10 minutes to 150.
tips: Schedule logins before your bar caps if practical; capped natural regeneration is lost opportunity.
Compare training, attacks and paid services by useful outcome per energy, not gross cash alone.

sections.title: Nerve
facts: Nerve regenerates by one every five minutes; bonuses can make the displayed maximum differ from natural nerve.
tips: Track crime skill separately from bar size when deciding what to attempt.
Spend naturally regenerated nerve before buying more; measure material losses and failures too.

sections.title: Happiness
facts: Above-maximum happiness resets at quarter-hour boundaries; it affects gym gains and Crimes 2.0 progression.
tips: Prepare supplies and energy before raising happiness; leave time to complete training before the next reset.
Do not copy a costly happy-jump recipe without comparing its cost per stat gain for your own account.

sections.title: Life
facts: Life normally regenerates by 5% of maximum every five minutes; full life alone does not remove hospital time.
tips: Check life, hospital status and medical cooldown independently.
Keep compatible medical supplies available before a planned attack session.

sections.title: Chain
facts: A chain starts with ten successful attacks in five minutes, then needs a successful hit before its timer expires.
tips: Coordinate backup hitters so one failed attack does not leave the timer unattended.
Follow the faction's bonus-hit allocation instead of racing a teammate for a milestone.

sections.title: Mail Events & Awards
facts: Awards may change with crime-system migration; the wiki flags some requirements as incomplete.
tips: Use your own current awards screen to verify an unlock before spending resources for it.
Read faction mail and transaction events before deleting messages that could explain a missing payment.

sections.title: Areas
facts: The sidebar links to the main activity areas; access can depend on your current game state.
tips: If a page is unavailable, check travel, jail and hospital state before assuming an outage.
Learn the city quick links for common purchases rather than following strangers' shortened URLs.

sections.title: Home
facts: Torn's Home page supports rearranging and minimising information boxes.
tips: Keep bars, education, perks and useful activity summaries near the top.
Treat helper snapshots as dated observations and confirm important changes in game.

sections.title: Items / Inventory
facts: Items include equipment, tools, materials and consumables, with different uses and trading restrictions.
tips: Check category filters and whether an item is equipped or committed elsewhere before assuming it vanished.
Read an item's effect and current market listing before using, discarding or bulk-selling it.

sections.title: City
facts: The city map supports item finds and faction-territory information.
tips: Separate collecting finds from shopping; assess unfamiliar items before selling them.
Repeated clicking is not a substitute for learning the relevant page or verifying an item's purpose.

sections.title: Job
facts: Starter jobs award daily pay, work stats and job points; explicitly passive specials can remain after leaving.
tips: Plan promotions around work-stat requirements rather than choosing a job only for today's wage.
Compare the long-term unlock with a player company's pay, training policy and activity expectations.

sections.title: Gym
facts: Gyms have different training multipliers and unlock through gym experience plus membership purchases.
tips: Check the next gym's multipliers before paying; specialise only when it fits your stat plan.
Record before-and-after stats to evaluate your own training budget rather than trusting a fixed beginner threshold.

sections.title: Properties
facts: Rent is prepaid; tenants can incur staff upkeep, and a rented property's vault is inaccessible.
tips: Compare rent plus staff cost per day rather than only the headline rental price.
Read upgrades and remaining lease duration before paying for housing intended for travel.

sections.title: Education
facts: Courses can have prerequisites and drug-related expulsion can force a restart.
tips: Queue your next course choice in advance and set a reminder for completion.
Link education to a specific unlock or passive perk, and monitor addiction before an important course ends.

sections.title: Crimes
facts: Crimes 2.0 has hidden crime experience and separate, visible skill for each crime.
tips: Use the expanded Crimes 2.0 chapter here; do not apply old Crimes 1.0 nerve ladders to the new system.
Decide whether your session targets skill, unique outcomes or cash before choosing subcrimes.

sections.title: Missions
facts: Contract standing changes with success, failure and declining; accepting every contract is not always beneficial.
tips: Read every condition before accepting, including target, weapon and finishing-result requirements.
Price supplies and energy against the reward, and leave a time buffer for unavailable targets.

sections.title: Newspaper
facts: The newspaper includes articles, job listings, property markets and bounties.
tips: Check publication dates so an old announcement is not mistaken for the current event.
Use official article and announcement links when verifying a claim repeated in chat.

sections.title: Jail
facts: Busting success depends on several factors, and repeated attempts close together can reduce success rates.
tips: Compare waiting, bail and asking for a bust before repeatedly spending nerve.
Use jail time productively where possible; do not deliberately fail crimes just to reach a jail gym.

sections.title: Hospital
facts: Hospital time and medical cooldown govern different restrictions; several exit methods have exceptions.
tips: Budget the cooldown cost of each medical item instead of using the strongest item automatically.
Before paying for a revive, confirm your settings allow it and agree whether payment depends on success.

sections.title: Casino
facts: Casino tokens and casino-job points are different resources.
tips: Treat casino play as optional entertainment with a hard loss budget, not a dependable income plan.
Do not raise stakes to recover losses; use in-game self-exclusion if gambling stops being enjoyable.

sections.title: Hall Of Fame
facts: Some rankings show your position without exposing other players' private battle-stat identities.
tips: Use personal progress over time rather than comparing your first week with veteran accounts.
Do not infer exact hidden stats from a rank, title or level alone.

sections.title: Factions / My Faction
facts: Faction membership provides shared resources, upgrades and coordinated activities.
tips: Compare obligations and payout policies alongside perks before accepting an invitation.
Ask when withdrawal requests are handled, especially if you intend to use the faction vault.

sections.title: To join or not to join a faction
facts: New members normally begin with a 72-hour Recruit period and limited access.
tips: Ask which benefits are available immediately and which require full membership.
Choose an activity schedule that fits real life; an impressive perk list is not enough if attendance rules do not fit.

sections.title: Organized Crimes
facts: OCs 2.0 have planning and execution stages with role-specific requirements.
tips: Ask which role suits your success chance and bring the listed equipment before committing.
Check readiness before flying or scheduling an absence; coordinate replacements early.

sections.title: Recruit Citizens
facts: Referral rewards are tied to genuine referred players' progression.
tips: Invite people who want to play and help them understand the game rather than promising easy money.
Never create a second account to obtain referral rewards.

sections.title: Calendar
facts: Events may use player-selected time slots; dates in old guides are not an authoritative schedule.
tips: Copy both start and end times from your own current calendar into a reminder.
Check whether a bonus applies at departure, consumption, claim or another event-specific action.

sections.title: Community Events
facts: Community competitions and seasonal systems have their own participation rules.
tips: Read deadlines, eligibility and reward delivery conditions before sending an entry.
Keep the original announcement or entry receipt when a host promises a prize.

sections.title: Lists
facts: Friends, enemies and targets serve different organisational purposes.
tips: Use short, consistent descriptions so the list remains searchable months later.
Review notes after a player's status or your relationship changes.

sections.title: Friends List
facts: Friends can have custom descriptions and status filters.
tips: Save reliable traders, mentors and service providers with a note explaining the relationship.
Keep payment terms in an actual conversation; a friendly label is not a guarantee.

sections.title: Enemies List
facts: Enemies-list settings can block listed players from purchases across several markets.
tips: Review purchase-block settings before using the list merely as a convenient bookmark.
Keep factual notes; avoid turning an old dispute into an accidental ongoing trade restriction.

sections.title: Chats
facts: Public, group and private channels have different access and conduct rules.
tips: Choose the correct channel before posting a question, trade advert or faction instruction.
Never paste credentials into a chat, even if someone claims to be support.

sections.title: Chats Settings Panel
facts: Channel access depends partly on membership and game state.
tips: Review notification settings and mute noisy channels during time-sensitive activity.
If a channel disappears, first check whether your faction, company or travel state changed.

sections.title: New Player Chat
facts: Access ends at level 13 or after 336 hours of accumulated play time.
tips: Use the protected channel to ask basic questions while eligible.
After access ends, use suitable help forums or faction mentors rather than trying to regain it through another account.

sections.title: Global
facts: Global is for social discussion; trade advertising is not permitted there.
tips: Move sales offers to the appropriate trade channel or forum.
Avoid repeating a message when nobody replies; provide better context instead.

sections.title: Trade Chat
facts: Trade chat is for adverts; the documented limits are one message per 60 seconds and 125 characters.
tips: Fit item, price basis and contact terms into a concise advert.
Check your current channel rules before posting, rather than following old advice to spam advertisements.

sections.title: Faction
facts: Faction chat is tied to membership.
tips: Confirm war orders and targets with the current organiser rather than an old pinned conversation.
Keep important payout or supply agreements in a durable written message too.

sections.title: Company
facts: Company chat provides a shared channel for that company's members.
tips: Use it to coordinate trains, stock needs or absences with the director.
Do not assume an informal chat promise overrides the published company policy.

sections.title: Hospital / Jail / Travel
facts: These channels appear and disappear with the relevant game state.
tips: Explain your location and need clearly when requesting a service.
Verify the provider's Torn ID and price before sending cash or items.

sections.title: Misc
facts: Torn Time follows UTC rather than a daylight-saving local timezone.
tips: Write deadlines with a timezone and date instead of saying only tonight.
Keep a small emergency float and relevant supplies before long or scheduled activities.

sections.title: Time - TCT
facts: TCT is UTC year-round; India Standard Time is UTC plus 5 hours 30 minutes.
tips: For example, 12:00 TCT is 17:30 IST; account for date changes around midnight.
Use an actual timezone-aware calendar for international teammates rather than memorising every offset.

sections.title: NPC Looting
facts: NPC loot uses a contribution-based lottery; joining a fight does not guarantee an item.
tips: Check the NPC's current loot level and a coordinated attack plan before spending energy.
A beginner should compare the cost of participation with reliable training or levelling progress.

basic-elements.summary: A complete interface tour with current resource mechanics and advice for every original section.
corrections: Happy helps Crimes 2.0 skill/experience gains; this is not the same as improving success chance.
Old city-find and chat assumptions should be checked against the current systems.
checklist: Check timers before buying a cure or booster.
Keep education and training aligned with one useful unlock.
Use live in-game information when helper data is old or incomplete.

extras.title: A resource check before expensive actions
facts: Energy, nerve, happy and their cooldowns do not all refill or reset in the same way.
tips: Before consuming anything expensive, check current amount, cap, next timer and the action you will immediately take.
Do not mistake an estimated countdown for a verified live value after acting elsewhere in Torn.

sections.title: The Magic Number
facts: Level 15 unlocks overseas travel; visible level and combat strength are not interchangeable.
tips: Pursue reliable wins rather than the highest-level name on a list.
After unlocking travel, reassess training and income instead of assuming permanent attack-only play is optimal.

sections.title: Levelling Targets
facts: Leaving after a win yields more level experience than mugging or hospitalising the same target.
tips: Use your actual attack history to build a small list of repeatable wins.
Check current status before spending energy; inactivity and historical stats do not guarantee an easy fight.

sections.title: Initial Preparation
facts: Equipment includes melee, firearms, temporary items and armour; damage and accuracy matter alongside item names.
tips: Equip what you bought and check ammunition if using a firearm.
Borrow faction gear or compare inexpensive upgrades before spending most of your cash on prestige equipment.

sections.title: The Housing Situation
facts: A lease fixes its agreed terms; staff still create upkeep costs.
tips: Choose housing you can afford throughout the levelling period rather than just on day one.
Keep enough for supplies and a later travel setup instead of exhausting your float on rent.

sections.title: Getting your happy up
facts: Ecstasy doubles current happiness but has overdose risk; surplus happiness has a quarter-hour reset.
tips: Prepare the full sequence before using expensive happiness items.
Use a cheaper training session if an overdose or missed timer would derail your budget.

sections.title: The Lists of Levelling Targets
facts: Target catalogues are references, not guarantees of unchanged stats or availability.
tips: Use Torn Helper's Baldr and Community filters, then confirm a target through recent observations and results.
Avoid assuming a ten-day-inactive submission is permanently inactive; its verification date matters.

sections.title: Attacking the Levelling Targets
facts: A normal attack costs 25 energy and has a 25-turn, five-minute limit.
tips: Stop repeatedly attacking a target that you cannot defeat; diagnose accuracy, damage, life and equipment first.
For levelling, choose Leave deliberately after the win rather than reflexively selecting a cash option.

level15.summary: Reach travel access through affordable preparation and reliable wins, not a fixed stat or cash target.
corrections: The archived equipment prices and 500-stat suggestion are examples, not current prices or a guaranteed combat threshold.
checklist: Equip affordable gear and arrange medical supplies.
Test a suitable target and record the result.
Use Leave for level experience and take available level upgrades while pursuing level 15.

extras.title: When a target stops being profitable
facts: Battle outcome depends on more than displayed level; no fixed beginner stat total guarantees a win.
tips: After repeated failures, compare turns, accuracy, damage and medical cost, then train or pick another target.
Do not keep spending energy simply because a target appeared on a respected list.

sections.title: Prerequisites
facts: Travel inventory and baggage rules changed in June 2026.
tips: Check your actual travel screen for capacity, usable supplies and restrictions before your first flight.
Compare the cost of your entire round trip with the expected net sale proceeds.

sections.title: Renting Island
facts: Rented vault access is unavailable even if the property listing includes a vault upgrade.
tips: Verify an airstrip is included and budget ongoing staff upkeep separately from rent.
Do not buy an island solely to unlock a benefit you could access more cheaply through a suitable lease.

sections.title: Hiring a Pilot
facts: An airstrip and pilot give access to the corresponding travel method; an airstrip alone is not enough.
tips: Check staff are actually hired and the intended flight option is active before departing.
Record recurring pilot and property costs when comparing routes.

sections.title: Why you should only run flowers/plushies at start
facts: Flowers and plushies have museum-set demand; newer contraband has different pricing and risk.
tips: Treat flowers and plushies as a simple starting strategy, not a rule that no other item can be profitable.
Test demand and net margin on a small shipment before committing your full working capital.

sections.title: Flower/Plushie Running
facts: Default baggage is 10; the airstrip/WLT/business base is 15, before applicable bonuses.
tips: Use displayed capacity, round-trip time, current purchase price and after-fee resale proceeds.
Plan a fallback item and a maximum waiting time if the intended shop is empty.

after15.summary: Travel with the current baggage rules and calculate net income for your own schedule.
corrections: The 2026 revision increased standard capacity and reduced suitcase bonuses; the archived +4 large-suitcase advice is outdated.
Black-market pricing is variable; a saved screenshot is not a current quote.
checklist: Verify the active travel method, capacity and recurring housing cost.
Check destination stock and a fallback purchase before flying.
Compare net profit per round-trip hour and sell without leaving unnecessary cash exposed.

extras.title: Foreign shop pricing and inventory
facts: Contraband Importation introduced separate General Store, Arms Dealer and Black Market shops; drugs and contraband have variable prices.
tips: Treat saved foreign prices as observations, and verify the shop price before buying.
Leave room for the items you intend to bring and check the travel inventory rather than relying on an old capacity screenshot.

tables.title: Current baggage reference
rows: Airstrip plus pilot / WLT / Business Class base
These alternative bases do not add together.
Only the largest applicable suitcase counts.
Use your own active faction perks.
Do not assume a flower bonus applies to all goods.

sections.title: NPO - Valour
facts: Its recruitment thread describes Valour as an entry-level branch, but current acceptance and perks must be confirmed.
tips: Ask which requirements have exceptions for players below level 15.
Read the current first post and contact admissions before planning around a quoted perk.

sections.title: WTF Family
facts: The imported family description is historical; a family name does not verify the policies of each branch.
tips: Ask which actual faction ID fits your goals and skill level.
Compare each branch's war schedule, bank access and membership conditions separately.

sections.title: WTF
facts: Current recruitment availability and perks were not independently verified for this historical entry.
tips: Confirm the faction ID through a current recruiter or profile.
Request current expectations and payout terms instead of relying on the archived description.

sections.title: WTF Medical
facts: The old guide describes a medical branch; present revive benefits and recruitment status are unverified.
tips: Ask the current energy cost of reviving and whether Brain Surgeon is required before joining.
Check contracts, training support and whether failed revive attempts are paid.

sections.title: WTF Healers
facts: The historical healer listing is not a current offer of membership or a verified perk guarantee.
tips: Compare revive-training support with the requirements of your current job progression.
Ask about activity obligations and how contract revenue is distributed.

sections.title: Toxic Spawn
facts: A community beginner-faction list references Toxic Spawn; this does not verify a present vacancy.
tips: Check the current profile, recruiter and requirements before applying.
Ask how beginners progress to another branch and whether any costs or obligations apply.

sections.title: New Sith Order
facts: The recruitment thread distinguishes a war-focused family branch; historic beginner suitability is not assured.
tips: Ask which branch currently accepts your battle stats and schedule.
Confirm whether the listed war requirements and supplies policy fit your budget.

sections.title: TORNado
facts: A faction recruitment thread exists, but an old thread title cannot establish current vacancies or perks.
tips: Inspect the current first post and date of the recruiter's latest response.
Request written terms for training, supplies and withdrawals before depositing significant funds.

sections.title: We Are Rising
facts: No sufficiently current recruitment offer was verified for this archived name and ID.
tips: Use the numeric faction ID in the original source to avoid confusing a rename or similarly named group.
Confirm leadership, membership rules and current recruitment status directly in Torn.

sections.title: NNGO Deja 2
facts: Current recruitment and benefits were not verified for this historical directory entry.
tips: Check whether the faction has been renamed, reorganised or moved to a different role.
Compare current active perks and participation requirements before treating it as a beginner option.

factions-new-players.summary: Evaluate a faction by current fit and terms rather than a historical name or benefit list.
corrections: Named entries are historical leads. Present recruitment, ownership, requirements and perks are not guaranteed.
checklist: Compare active upgrades and participation expectations.
Read the current recruitment thread and confirm the exact faction ID.
Agree supply, payout and vault-withdrawal policies before committing.

extras.title: Current faction selection checklist
facts: Faction resources, upgrades and membership terms differ; a historical directory is not a live offer.
tips: Ask for active training/travel perks, war frequency, supply policy, payout deductions and withdrawal availability.
Prefer a clear, sustainable fit over a recruitment promise you cannot independently verify.

sections.title: Mugging
facts: Mugging takes a variable proportion of exposed cash and can be modified by perks.
tips: Plan the cash-storage action before a predictable incoming payment.
Do not treat a high net worth, hospital plan or small previous mug as proof that your next payment is safe.

sections.title: Mug Protection
facts: Post-mug protected cash decays over 12 hours; moving protected funds can reduce that protection.
tips: Do not repeatedly move funds under the assumption that the original protected amount will remain intact.
Treat protection as a loss-limiting mechanic, not a reason to leave future sale proceeds exposed.

sections.title: Cash Storage
facts: Storage choices differ in access, lockup, volatility and counterparty risk.
tips: Split emergency spending money from investments and money needed on a known date.
Write down your exit route before depositing, buying an asset or starting a trade.

sections.title: Piggy Bank
facts: The beginner piggy bank is a one-time opportunity; withdrawing destroys it and puts the balance in hand.
tips: Check George's mission store early rather than assuming you can buy one later.
Arrange the next storage destination before breaking it.

sections.title: Ghost Trades
facts: An unfinished trade can be cancelled; completed acceptance transfers its contents.
tips: Do not confuse temporary trade holding with interest-bearing or unlimited-duration banking.
Use a trusted counterparty and an explicit agreement that the holding trade must not be completed.

sections.title: How to set a ghost trade?
facts: The initiating player has the final acceptance step in direct trading.
tips: Confirm the recipient ID and purpose, then leave the trade unfinished and monitor its state.
Keep a separate reminder to review the holding arrangement; do not leave critical cash dependent on an abandoned conversation.

sections.title: City Bank
facts: Time deposits offer several durations with changing APR; matured funds can remain in the bank until withdrawn.
tips: Compare the current term return and when you need the money, not merely the largest interest figure.
Keep a reserve outside a locked deposit so an urgent expense does not force a worse borrowing decision.

sections.title: Cayman Island
facts: Offshore interest uses the month's lowest qualifying balance, and access requires being abroad.
tips: Include travel and time costs when comparing it with other storage choices.
Do not assume a late-month deposit earns a full month's interest.

sections.title: Stocks
facts: Stock sales have a 0.1% fee and trading is restricted in hospital, jail and transit.
tips: Stocks are not a risk-free cash vault: price changes and inability to access them can matter more than the fee.
Avoid needing an immediate sale to pay for a war, rental or other deadline.

sections.title: Points
facts: Points are a separate currency and must normally be exchanged through their own market.
tips: Compare the buy/sell spread before using points as temporary value storage.
Keep planned refill points separate from a speculative resale position.

sections.title: Items
facts: Different items have different markets, restrictions and liquidity.
tips: Store value only in items you understand well enough to price and sell.
Calculate the cash you could actually receive after selling costs instead of using an estimated inventory value.

sections.title: Property Vaults
facts: A tenant cannot access a rented property's vault.
tips: Check ownership, shared access and current capacity before treating a vault as available storage.
Do not pay extra rent for vault access you will not receive.

sections.title: Faction Vault
facts: Faction resources are controlled by members with the relevant permissions.
tips: Ask who can authorise a withdrawal and what happens while officers are offline.
Keep a personal record of deposits and avoid entrusting money you cannot afford to wait for.

sections.title: Company Vaults
facts: A company vault is part of a player-run business, not your personal bank.
tips: Keep operating cash separate from personal money in your records.
Consider director access, sale terms and business liabilities before using a company as storage.

sections.title: Winning the lottery / Slots / Big Money Quick Storage
facts: Some large receipts use cashier's checks while other payouts can create immediate wallet exposure.
tips: Before claiming, identify the exact payout mechanism and prepare a storage destination.
Avoid announcing a windfall publicly until you have dealt with the practical cash exposure.

sections.title: Slots Win
facts: Casino activity can create large gains or losses; it is not a reliable savings method.
tips: After an unusual win, stop and protect the proceeds instead of increasing the stake.
Do not assume a slots payout follows the same claim process as a lottery cheque.

sections.title: Lottery Win
facts: Lottery winnings are cashier's checks that automatically credit after 24 hours if not collected.
tips: Set a reminder before the automatic-credit deadline and decide where the money will go.
Verify the bank record itself rather than following an unexpected message claiming you won.

sections.title: Investing your winnings
facts: Bank rates vary and stock prices can fall; a quoted return is not a guarantee.
tips: Separate training, housing and emergency budgets before investing the remainder.
Avoid buying several benefit blocks at once without comparing their marginal yield and loss of liquidity.

money-storage.summary: Compare wallet exposure, access time, lockup, volatility and trust for every storage method.
corrections: A rented property does not provide vault access.
Stocks can lose value and are unavailable in some game states; they are not an instant guaranteed vault.
Mug protection can change when protected cash is moved.
checklist: Plan the destination before a large receipt.
Keep a separate operating float for foreseeable expenses.
Set reminders for deposits, temporary holdings and automatic cheque credit.

extras.title: A plan for a predictable cash receipt
facts: Different payout mechanisms can put money in hand immediately or after a claim deadline.
tips: Decide the claim time, destination and required access in advance; perform the storage step before unrelated browsing.
Keep the action manual and confirm the resulting balance in game rather than trusting a helper notification.

sections.title: For Newbies
facts: Early earning methods consume different combinations of time, energy and capital.
tips: Choose a method that funds your next useful unlock without consuming every resource needed for growth.
Track net proceeds and time spent for a week before deciding a method is worth scaling.

sections.title: Selling Losses/Slutting
facts: Paid losses use attack energy that could otherwise support levelling or gym training.
tips: Agree quantity, weapon conditions, proof and payment timing before the first hit.
Compare the net pay after recovery costs with the progress you are giving up; do a small trial with an unfamiliar buyer.

sections.title: City Shops
facts: Shop purchase cost and player resale value are separate prices.
tips: Check today's stock and demand before buying; an old beer or candy margin is not a current quote.
Include sales fees and any unsold inventory when calculating whether the daily run helped.

sections.title: Odd Jobs
facts: Player services rely on a specific agreement rather than a built-in salary guarantee.
tips: Define a small deliverable, payment amount, deadline and acceptance standard.
Keep work inside Torn's rules and avoid services involving account access or real-money exchanges.

sections.title: Advertising
facts: Trade and Global have different permitted uses; old spam-based advice is unsuitable.
tips: Use the correct channel and measure genuine replies or completed sales, not message volume.
Agree the placement and duration before paying for another player's advertising service.

sections.title: Company Employee Finding
facts: Companies need staff suited to their positions and operating model.
tips: Ask the director for work-stat, activity and retention requirements before searching.
Agree what counts as a successful referral and when the fee becomes payable; do not promise a job on the director's behalf.

sections.title: Community Events
facts: Event eligibility and rewards depend on each organiser's published conditions.
tips: Enter only when the likely reward or enjoyment justifies the entry cost.
Save proof of submission and check whether the organiser has a clear payout process.

sections.title: Fun & Forum / Discord Servers
facts: Off-site communities do not replace Torn's game rules or account-security controls.
tips: Verify invitations through a known profile or official thread rather than a random direct message.
Do not pay an upfront verification fee or disclose keys to claim an unexpected prize.

sections.title: City Map
facts: City finds can spawn after daily activity; more clicking does not produce more spawns.
tips: Collect finds during a short routine and value unusual items before selling.
Do not build an income budget around rare windfalls.

sections.title: GFX Design
facts: Creative work for Torn assets still needs to respect the game's trading rules.
tips: Agree size, format, revisions, delivery and usage rights before starting a commission.
Use a small paid milestone for custom work and retain previews or receipts to document completion.

sections.title: Responsible gambling
facts: Gambling outcomes are uncertain; token availability does not create a positive-return income method.
tips: Exclude gambling winnings from the budget needed for rent, training and supplies.
Set an affordable entertainment limit and do not use progression money to chase a loss.

sections.title: Companies
facts: Directors manage staff, stock and advertising; gross revenue is not net business profit.
tips: Request operating records and liabilities before buying a company.
Stress-test a bad week of wages, advertising and inventory costs before committing your capital.

sections.title: City Bank
facts: The normal investment ceiling is $2 billion; a qualifying Oil Rig benefit can raise it.
tips: Use the current bank offer to compare your next investment, keeping known expenses liquid.
Do not pool or borrow money merely because an old guide shows an attractive historic rate.

sections.title: Intermediate
facts: Service and faction income depend on skill, opportunities, terms and actual participation.
tips: Select a repeatable method that fits your schedule rather than adopting every veteran activity.
Measure net earnings alongside energy consumption and time availability.

sections.title: Reviving
facts: Reviving unlocks through Brain Surgeon; attempts consume energy even when they fail.
tips: Agree success-based or attempt-based payment before a contract starts.
Use the displayed success chance and your energy cost to estimate expected pay per energy.

sections.title: Flower/Plushie Running
facts: Foreign stock availability and local resale demand can change between departures.
tips: Rank routes by net profit per round-trip hour, including waiting and selling time.
Try more than one buyer and keep a fallback route instead of relying on yesterday's highest margin.

sections.title: Stocks Benefit Blocks
facts: Passive benefits have a holding period; active dividends need claiming before another cycle progresses.
tips: Set collection reminders and check the marginal cost of the next increment.
Value an item dividend at a realistic after-fee sale price, not a headline market estimate.

sections.title: Bounties
facts: Claiming a bounty requires a qualifying hospitalisation; a high bounty does not imply an easy target.
tips: Check target strength and availability before committing recovery items and energy.
Compare likely net reward with repeated-failure risk and the opportunity cost of training.

sections.title: Ranked Warring
facts: Weekly ranked-war templates were introduced in November 2026; enlistment shows the applicable rules.
tips: Read this week's template before planning hits or relying on an old score target.
Agree your faction's payout formula and expense deductions before the war, then retain the report.

sections.title: Building Flower/Plushie Sets
facts: The History bachelor unlocks museum exchanges; complete flower or plushie sets exchange for points.
tips: Price the entire set, including its least convenient item, against the current value of the points received.
Include selling costs, available cash and time spent assembling sets rather than assuming every set is profitable.

sections.title: Events/Competitions
facts: Special bonuses have event-specific start and end conditions.
tips: Check your own event slot before buying supplies or scheduling a large action.
Budget for the ordinary outcome; a rare event prize should remain upside rather than expected income.

sections.title: Mugging
facts: Mug results are variable and affected by protection and perks.
tips: Do not infer a guaranteed target balance from a visible sale or an old net-worth figure.
Consider retaliation, failed attacks and training opportunity cost when deciding whether an attempt is worthwhile.

sections.title: Advanced
facts: Trading and businesses introduce more capital and liquidity risk than a simple service sale.
tips: Keep a written ledger of cost basis, fees, stock levels and cash tied up.
Scale only after you can explain where profit comes from and what would make the plan fail.

sections.title: Trading
facts: Item-market sales carry fees; direct trades and bazaars have different processes and exposure.
tips: Calculate margin after fees, price movement, slow stock and the value of your own time.
Make a small test purchase before expanding into an unfamiliar item category.

sections.title: Stocks
facts: Share-price gains are distinct from dividend benefits and neither guarantees profit.
tips: Track realised proceeds after the selling fee and keep capital for near-term obligations out of a speculative position.
Do not present a guessed price pattern as a predictable trading signal.

sections.title: Mercenaries
facts: Outside combat services depend on game restrictions and a buyer's agreed qualifying conditions.
tips: Specify eligible targets, finish result, evidence, payment and exclusions before accepting work.
Use reports to reconcile completed work; do not assume every visible hit qualifies under a faction's contract.

money-making.summary: Choose earnings by net return, time, resource use and downside risk.
corrections: Old sale-price and hourly-income examples are not live earning guarantees.
The ordinary item-market sales fee is 5%; a route or trade must account for its actual selling channel.
Ranked-war templates now make checking the current enlistment rules important.
checklist: Choose one repeatable earning method and record the full costs.
Keep progression energy and near-term cash needs in your plan.
Scale only when completed results support the expected margin.

extras.title: Marginal return versus total return
facts: An additional investment can have a different cost and yield from the first one.
tips: Compare the next block or upgrade on its own additional cost rather than averaging it with a cheaper earlier purchase.
Keep realistic sale prices and an adverse scenario in the worksheet before committing money.

tables.title: Net return worksheet (editorial calculation)
rows: Sale proceeds after fees − purchase cost
Use the fee of the actual selling channel.
Quantity × unit margin − other trip costs
Include paid travel and allocated recurring costs.
Include both flights, waiting and selling time.
Illustrative example, not a price quote
Expected net pay ÷ total energy spent
Include unsuccessful attempts and unpaid work.

sections.title: A Criminal Primer
facts: The player-authored Criminal Primer includes an October 2026 Arson update; it remains community guidance.
tips: Use the crime-specific notes below and compare them with the current interface and linked wiki.
Separate documented mechanics from community estimates of optimal profitability or progression.

extras.title: Search for Cash
facts: All six searches cost two nerve. Beach and cemetery require unlock items; the fountain needs skill 75.
tips: Trash, subway and junkyard have different environmental conditions; use the current on-screen cues rather than a fixed best crime rule.
Treat unique-outcome hunting as a separate goal from short-term cash and check any required item before repeating attempts.

extras.title: Bootlegging
facts: Copying, selling and an online store are separate activities. The store needs skill 50, the named web-design course and a computer.
tips: Count blank-DVD costs and the time needed to sell copied stock; copying alone does not realise cash profit.
Check production and remaining stock before spending more nerve on an already overfilled genre.

extras.title: Graffiti
facts: Area reputation changes independently and decays; the Paint Mask is its enhancer. Some areas require a crew unlock.
tips: Build an area deliberately rather than spreading early attempts everywhere.
Watch remaining paint and distinguish reputation goals from cash goals.

extras.title: Shoplifting
facts: Each shop has its own notoriety and security state. Notoriety falls over time; four nerve is used per attempt.
tips: Rotate or pause when local notoriety is costly, using the actual shop indicators.
Do not treat disabled cameras or a high skill level as a guarantee; budget for lost supplies and failures.

extras.title: Pickpocketing
facts: Targets vary by type, body and current distraction; availability does not mean suitability for your skill.
tips: Choose manageable targets and watch their expiry timers instead of rushing every new row.
Track failures by target type so your next session uses your own evidence rather than a universal promise of safety.

extras.title: Card Skimming
facts: Installation uses a card skimmer and spy camera; details become usable on recovery, and devices can be lost.
tips: Treat longer placement as a return-versus-loss-risk decision, not an automatic improvement.
Keep a placement log and include replacement equipment in your cash-per-nerve estimate.

extras.title: Burglary
facts: Scout, case and burglarize are distinct actions. Casing confidence fades; a target's recommended item unlocks its unique reward.
tips: Plan enough nerve to finish a chosen target rather than accumulating more locations than you will use.
Check the recommendation and current confidence before the final step; focused scouting has a higher nerve cost than ordinary scouting.

extras.title: Hustling
facts: Audience interest, suspicion and each game's technique affect play. Shill and pickpocket helpers unlock at higher skill.
tips: Develop a game deliberately and watch the audience rather than repeatedly choosing the win action.
Include intentional losses and helper collection costs when comparing actual session profit.

extras.title: Disposal
facts: Jobs arrive daily and can only be attempted once. Method choice and required consumables vary by job.
tips: Read the job and compare the available methods before choosing; the most expensive method is not automatically best.
Check supplies first and preserve a record of method and outcome to improve future decisions.

extras.title: Cracking
facts: This in-game minigame requires Introduction to Computing and a computer. Wrong character guesses can lock further guesses.
tips: Treat this solely as a Torn minigame; no real accounts or external passwords are involved.
Compare rig-upgrade costs with the jobs available to your skill and avoid wasting guesses without a reason.

extras.title: Forgery
facts: Projects have multiple five-nerve steps, mixed reusable and consumed tools, and possible progress loss.
tips: Calculate all material costs for a finished item before starting a batch.
Stagger timed steps to match your normal logins instead of leaving many unfinished projects tying up supplies.

extras.title: Scamming
facts: The fictional crime uses an in-game address pool, responses and a reward-zone minigame.
tips: Only use the built-in Torn activity; never collect real email addresses or message real people for this guide.
Read the current cursor and zones, and budget the whole conversation rather than valuing only its final payout.

extras.title: Arson
facts: The in-game scenario uses different fire behaviour, client requirements and unlockable tools; Collect has its own final step.
tips: Keep this entirely within Torn's game interface and follow each fictional job's requirements.
Check what a consumable costs and whether the final condition is met before spending nerve on more actions.

extras.title: Crime progression without false guarantees
facts: Success, failure and critical failure affect progression differently; higher happiness helps progression rather than known success chance.
tips: Track profit, skill progression and unique outcomes separately. A cash strategy may not be the fastest skill strategy.
Use current subcrime indicators and keep a reserve for material losses; never label a method zero-risk without evidence.

crimes2.summary: Go beyond the old link-only page: progression basics plus thirteen crime-specific walkthrough notes.
corrections: Do not use the archived claim that the system has only twelve crimes as a current count.
Crime experience, individual crime skill, progression bonuses and hidden success formulas are different concepts.
checklist: Choose cash, progression or uniques as the purpose of the session.
Check current skill, required tools, consumables and conditions.
Record net proceeds and failures rather than assuming a higher nerve cost means better returns.

sections.title: Step 1: Visit the traders profile
facts: A direct trade can start from a player's profile or the inventory Trades interface.
tips: Verify the numeric ID rather than relying only on a similar-looking name or avatar.
For a new counterparty, agree price and quantity in a written message first.

sections.title: Step 2: Click on the trade icon
facts: The initiating party controls final completion after the other party accepts.
tips: Confirm you opened the intended trade instead of a send-money or send-item action.
Keep the agreed quote visible while reviewing the new transaction.

sections.title: Step 3: Fill Description on new trade panel
facts: A description labels the trade; it does not replace checking its actual contents.
tips: Use a specific description with item, quantity and agreed price basis.
Avoid vague labels that make two simultaneous trades hard to distinguish.

sections.title: Step 4: Use the Plus Buttons to add Items/Money
facts: Money and ordinary items are tradeable; points and shares are not normal direct-trade contents.
tips: Review both quantity and item variant before adding everything in your inventory.
Check the cash total using your own arithmetic rather than a screenshot sent by the other person.

sections.title: Step 5: Wait for the trader to add money
facts: The other party's acceptance locks the proposed contents against further changes.
tips: Treat an actual locked trade state as evidence; a chat message saying added is not enough.
Stop if the expected cash or item is missing, even when someone pressures you to hurry.

sections.title: Step 6: Trader has accepted, now its your turn
facts: Final acceptance includes a reconfirmation delay; cancellation remains possible before completion.
tips: Re-read both sides, the recipient and the exact amount during the final check.
Know where received cash will go before accepting a large sale.

how-to-set-trade.summary: A six-step transaction checklist with identity, contents and final-acceptance checks.
corrections: A description or chat promise does not prove payment has been added.
Points and shares cannot be placed into an ordinary direct trade.
checklist: Agree a quote and verify the counterparty ID.
Review both sides of the actual locked trade.
Use the final confirmation to re-check the exact contents and plan for any cash received.

extras.title: If a transaction changes or feels wrong
facts: A direct trade can be cancelled before final completion.
tips: Stop and re-check the actual contents when the quote, item variant or recipient changes.
Do not complete under pressure; restart a clean transaction if the agreement is no longer clear.

sections.title: How Often should I run through pages
facts: Egg spawns are activity-independent; unfound eggs persist and can roll over into the next event.
tips: Browse manually at sensible intervals instead of hammering refresh to try to generate more eggs.
Use your calendar for the current event window; this guide does not mean a hunt is active today.

sections.title: How do I use scripts on Mobile Devices
facts: Scripts must follow Torn's current scripting rules; software must not auto-request hidden game pages or click rewards.
tips: Review a script's source and permissions, and use only tooling that fits the current rules and your browser.
Do not install an unfamiliar extension merely because a historic guide recommends it.

sections.title: Eggs Usage Guide
facts: Collected eggs are non-tradeable inventory items; using one adds six hours of booster cooldown.
tips: Time an egg for a clear goal and check cooldown room before consuming it.
Percentage-based rewards may be more useful later; compare waiting with the benefit you can use now.

easter.summary: Use the current hunt mechanics and item effects instead of pre-2023 farming advice.
corrections: Refreshing does not increase the activity-independent spawn rate.
Collected eggs are inventory items, not immediate rewards that must be used when found.
This is a seasonal reference, not a statement that Easter is active today.
checklist: Check the current calendar and your event slot.
Browse manually using permitted tools only.
Choose egg timing based on your own stats, resources and booster cooldown.

extras.title: Booster planning around an egg
facts: An egg uses six hours of booster cooldown; surplus happy still has its normal timing constraint.
tips: Reserve enough cooldown room and prepare the activity that will use the reward before consuming the egg.
Do not spend resources chasing a claimed rare spawn schedule or an unverified guaranteed colour.

Do your chosen crimes and supplies support it?

Compare using now with delaying for larger stats.
